title: Experts disagree on rule_gate_budget_ms (Part D)
context:
Chief architect: Not a real disagreement: both are adopted. Part D lets an edit through only when the budget runs out, and only because the turn-end check will run; so the marker must force that check and a marker that cannot be written must fail closed, and crashes, bad output, per-script timeouts and tampered scripts keep today's blocking outcome. Pick this option to accept the pair.

Target: rule_gate_budget_ms (Part D)
- security-auditor: an edit allowed on budget expiry is still checked before the turn can end: the completion seam runs every deterministic script whenever a pending-pre-mutation marker exists, even when classifyCompletionEnforcement would otherwise skip that session, and a marker that cannot be written makes the edit fail closed instead of allowed
- security-auditor: only running out of the budget allows the edit; a deterministic script that crashes, exits non-zero, prints unparseable output or hits its own 30 s timeout keeps today's outcome under strict, and tampered rule scripts (verifyRuleScriptsIntegrity) still block before the budget logic runs
